title: a verdict run on Windows re-runs its instrument under a confirmed seal, so a Windows clause is judged by the gate and not only by the builder
intention: The verdict gate's re-run of a ticket's instrument works on Windows, so a clause that only Windows can show is judged by the gate's own run and not only by the builder's validate run.
why: Measured 2026-11-19 on akiendell: `sail.py verdict 35bb99574043` and `sail.py verdict 1eeeab70c59e` were each refused by the gate because its re-run of `bin/cairn test <proof>` exited 2 with: cairn test --exec: refused — the instance seal is not confirmed (indeterminate: cannot build the instance seal: bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed); the command was not run. Windows has no seal, so the gate can never confirm a green-on-Windows clause itself; it is measured only by the builder's own validate run (Law 3). The earlier instance 3a38e2e1cfe0 got around it by verdicting its Windows clause on Linux (berth verdict-20261113T024209, PROVED 11-13). Related: 56b61c10bdbe builds the Windows instance seal and is at TICKETME.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured: a Windows green measured by the builder alone is a claim); Law 8 (prove, then trust: the verdict is the peer's check that the hand did not write); Law 7 (the refusal is loud and stays a refusal).
how: A hypothesis, measured by clause 1: the gate's re-run of a ticket's instrument is accepted on Windows once the tester can confirm a seal there (the build reads 56b61c10bdbe before choosing between waiting on that seal and a gate-side change). Red-first proof under cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/proofs/, one tooth per clause, PROVES declared. No exemption: a refused re-run stays a refusal and a builder's validate run does not stand in for it.

clauses.claim: on Windows the verdict gate's re-run of a green proof returns exit 0 and the verdict artifact lands, where today the same call exits 2 with the instance-seal refusal
on Windows the gate's re-run of a red proof verdicts fail with the proof's own output as evidence, not the seal refusal
when no seal can be confirmed the gate still refuses, loud and recorded, naming the seal line, and writes no pass

decisions.text: D1: the verdict gate's instrument re-run is accepted on Windows under a confirmed seal; the build decides whether that is the 56b61c10bdbe seal or a gate-side change, and records it.
D2: the red-first proof drives the gate's re-run against a scratch proof and a fake seal state, one tooth per clause, PROVES declared.

measured.saw: sail.py verdict 35bb99574043 and 1eeeab70c59e on akiendell each refused: the re-run of bin/cairn test exited 2 with 'the instance seal is not confirmed (indeterminate: cannot build the instance seal: bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed); the command was not run'
